summary: Sodus Bay light on Lake Ontario: 1825 stone tower, 1871 limestone tower, main light to 1901; a Coast Guard station until 1973; a museum since 1985.

lens.where: tower (LighthouseFriends; the USLHS record gives third-and-a-half order as current)

structures.note: Attached to the 1871 tower; museum run by the Sodus Bay Historical Society (LighthouseFriends).
Attached to the dwelling. LighthouseFriends: just over fifty feet tall, focal plane seventy feet. USLHS record: 70 ft.
Stone tower on the west pier (LighthouseFriends; USLHS 'est. 1837'). Frame towers from 1872; inner beacon rebuilt 1895 (LighthouseFriends).

staffing.note: Coast Guard closed the station in 1973; a Coast Guard commander continued to live in the lighthouse (LighthouseFriends).

access.note: Museum and tower open in season (LighthouseFriends; USLHS 'open to public').

visit.note: Seasonal hours 1 May to 31 October, Tuesday to Sunday, 10 a.m. to 5 p.m. (LighthouseFriends).

facts.agency: Town of Sodus (owner, per LighthouseFriends); Sodus Bay Historical Society (museum, under lease).

events.note: Stone dwelling and conical stone tower completed; ten lamps and nine-inch reflectors (LighthouseFriends).
Main bay light first lit in the 1825 tower (LighthouseFriends).
Ishmael D. Hill first keeper (roster; LighthouseFriends).
Bennett C. Fitzhugh appointed after Hill was disqualified (LighthouseFriends).
Entrance piers built, 1829 to 1834 (LighthouseFriends).
Stone pier tower built on the west pier, nearly thirty feet tall (LighthouseFriends; USLHS 'est. 1837').
Sixth-order lens placed in the pier light (LighthouseFriends).
Gale destroyed the pier beacon (LighthouseFriends).
Revolving fourth-order lens installed in the bay light (LighthouseFriends).
Pair of range lights replaced the destroyed pier beacon (LighthouseFriends).
Assistant keeper post added to the station (LighthouseFriends).
Limestone tower and two-story dwelling completed 30 June 1871 (LighthouseFriends; USLHS record: tower established 1871).
The 1825 tower and dwelling were replaced and demolished (LighthouseFriends).
Keeper's dwelling extensively repaired; much of it rebuilt (Light-House Board report).
Inner beacon on the west pier rebuilt on an improved model (LighthouseFriends).
Substantial and commodious beacon with a lantern built to replace the unserviceable old one 'in the previous year' (Light-House Board report for the fiscal year ended June 30, 1896).
Main light on the bluff permanently discontinued, June 1901 (Light-House Board report, item 66-68).
Fourth-order lens moved from the bay light to the outer pier tower, 10 June 1901 (LighthouseFriends).
Air fog signal set up on the outer light, 3 June 1926 (LighthouseFriends).
Assistant keeper Charles Plummer recognised for rescuing a boy and girl from drowning near the lighthouse (LighthouseFriends).
Present square pyramidal pierhead tower erected; new inner tower; electricity for light and fog signal (LighthouseFriends).
Coast Guard watch-stander Thomas Muchow aided a man who fell off the breakwall, 31 August 1964 (LighthouseFriends).
Coast Guard closed the station (LighthouseFriends).
Placed on the National Register (LighthouseFriends).
Transferred from the General Services Administration to the town, after a congressional effort (LighthouseFriends).
Sodus Bay Historical Society museum dedicated 4 July 1985 (LighthouseFriends).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record gives a 1825 stone tower (standing) and an establishment date of 1837 (USLHS). LighthouseFriends says the 1825 bay tower was demolished in 1871 and the stone pier tower was built on the west pier in 1837. The 1837 date belongs to the pier light; the record's 'standing' applies to the 1871 tower.

corrections.proposed: tower, limestone, built 1871, standing (1825 tower demolished 1871)
corrections.why: LighthouseFriends says the 1825 tower and dwelling were demolished for the 1871 tower. The USLHS record gives the standing tower as limestone, established 1871.

corrections.proposed: order 4 Fresnel in the bay light 1858-1901; order 6 in the pier light from 1854
corrections.why: LighthouseFriends dates the fourth-order lens to 1858 and says it was removed in 1901. The sources disagree on the 1871 lens; see notes.

notes_for_editor: (1) Tower height: LighthouseFriends says the 1871 tower stands just over fifty feet with a focal plane of seventy feet; the USLHS record gives tower and focal height both 70 ft; Wikipedia gives 45 ft (lead only, not cited). (2) Lens: LighthouseFriends says a fourth-order lens is displayed in the tower; the USLHS record gives 'THIRD AND HALF ORDER' as current and 'SIXTH ORDER' as original (1871); Wikipedia says 3.5 order (not cited). (3) Ownership: LighthouseFriends says Town of Sodus Point and also Town of Sodus; Wikipedia says Village of Sodus Point (not cited). Check the municipality. (4) Searches: Chronicling America for 1870-72 and for 1871-1901 Sodus items found nothing usable. The 1870 appropriation and the 1871 construction rest on LighthouseFriends alone; the official reports before 1891 are not in the local corpus. (5) Scan pages: the 1901 'main light discontinued' item is on scan p. 216 and the 'changed from sixth to fourth order' item is on scan p. 30. Printed pages not confirmed. Fiscal years now read from the title pages: the 1895 item is in the report for the fiscal year ended June 30, 1895 (scan p. 357); the 1896 item is in the report for the fiscal year ended June 30, 1896 (scan p. 155), which says the beacon work was 'in the previous year' and 'omitted in the Board's last annual report'. The FY1895 report already describes the inner west-pier beacon as rebuilt; the two reports are not reconciled and the story does not date the beacon more closely than 1895. (6) LighthouseFriends' account of Hill's petition and the 1829 disqualification was not checked against the petition. (7) Coast Guard staff after about 1960 appear only in the roster and in the 1964 rescue as LighthouseFriends reports it (public role). (8) The record's 1825 tower may be a mix of two structures in the sources; the story follows LighthouseFriends for the 1825 and 1871 towers.
